brief.headline: Tata Steel Deals Rs 28,000 Cr Asset Sale; Global Tech Selloff Weighs
brief.summary: Tata Steel approved the sale of its steel tubes, pipes, and colors businesses to APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 28,000 crore. Meanwhile, global equities face pressure following a -5.28% drop in the Nasdaq and crashing metal prices. Nifty 50 faces resistance near 26,000 after completing a nearly 2.2% weekly gain.

takeaways.text: Tata Steel approved selling its tubes, pipes, and colors divisions to APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 28,000 crore to streamline operations.
India engineering exports rose 36% year-on-year to $12.74 billion in October on strong shipments to the US.
Gold broke below $4,000 as rising bond yields and rate expectations triggered multi-month lows across precious and industrial metals.
US markets dropped sharply overnight, with the Nasdaq falling -5.28% amid concern over overtightening by the Fed and AI valuations.
Amazon is closing in on a $7.5bn acquisition of AI startup Decart to boost AWS computing power against Nvidia.

sections.india: Nifty 50 gained nearly 2.2% over a fourth consecutive winning week, facing resistance near 26,000. Tata Steel cleared the sale of two businesses to APL Apollo Tubes for ₹28K cr. Meanwhile, India's oil and gas import bill rose 60% year-on-year in October to $16 billion as Brent prices increased.
sections.world: US equities tumbled overnight with the Nasdaq dropping -5.28% and S&P 500 losing -3.70%. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that the Fed risks overtightening following recent inflation data. In commodities, Brent crude dropped -2.21% to 89.95 while Gold slid -4.62% to 3515.4.
sections.tech: Amazon is nearing a $7.5bn deal to acquire AI start-up Decart to enhance AWS capabilities. In regulatory developments, California's investigation into Nvidia covers potential criminal violations regarding chip sales. Meanwhile, Anthropic's team reported using AI tool Claude to solve the 166-year-old Riemann Hypothesis.

stories.title: Tata Steel to sell tubes, pipes business and Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for Rs 28,000 crore
stories.summary: Tata Steel approved the sale of its steel tubes and pipes business to APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 11,700 crore. The company also agreed to sell its entire stake in Tata Steel Colors for Rs 16,300 crore. Both transactions received approval from the board during a meeting held on Sunday. Tata Steel's operations in multiple locations will be transferred to APL Apollo on a slump sale basis.
stories.ai_summary: Tata Steel approved selling its tubes and pipes business and Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for Rs 28,000 crore. The transaction includes selling tubes for Rs 11,700 crore and its stake in Colors for Rs 16,300 crore.
stories.why_it_matters: Positive for Tata Steel debt reduction; expansion trigger for APL Apollo Tubes.

stories.title: India's oil, gas import bill jumps 60% in October as Brent nearly doubles; cooking-gas usage falls
stories.summary: India's net oil and gas import bill rose 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October as Brent crude prices nearly doubled. Crude imports cost $19.5 billion despite a modest increase in volumes, while LPG consumption and imports contracted sharply amid shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.ai_summary: India's net oil and gas import bill jumped 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October as Brent crude prices surged. Crude imports totaled $19.5 billion during the month.
stories.why_it_matters: Negative for current account deficit and currency pressures; increases input cost risk for OMCs.

stories.title: Shree Cement targets 100 MT capacity in 3-4 years on India growth bet
stories.summary: Shree Cement plans to expand its production capacity to over 100 million tonnes per annum within four years. The company aims for a growth rate of 9-10 percent, surpassing the industry average. They have announced significant investments in new plants across various states in India to support this expansion. Shree Cement is also growing its ready-mix concrete operations, planning to increase capacity significantly.
stories.ai_summary: Shree Cement plans to scale its production capacity to 100 MT within 3-4 years. The company targets a growth rate of 9-10 percent, outperforming the industry average.
stories.why_it_matters: Positive for cement industry volume outlook and capital goods suppliers.
